questions.q: Should a request body to create a new record include an `attributes` object or an `Id` field?
options: No — those only appear in what Salesforce sends back in a response, not in what you send to create a record
Yes, both are required on every create request
Only Id is required; attributes is optional
Only attributes is required; Id is optional
questions.explain: A create request body is just the flat field:value pairs you're setting — Salesforce adds attributes and assigns the Id itself, neither of which you send.

questions.q: How does a lookup (parent) relationship typically appear in a JSON request body?
options: As a nested object with its own totalSize and records array
As a simple field holding the parent record's ID, e.g. "AccountId": "001xx..."
It cannot be set through the REST API
As an array of related record IDs
questions.explain: A lookup field is just an ID value pointing to the parent record — much simpler than the nested shape of a child relationship query result.

questions.q: How does a child relationship (e.g. an Account's related Contacts) appear in a REST query response, as opposed to a lookup field?
options: Identically to a lookup field — just an ID
As a nested structure with its own totalSize, done, and records array, since it's a nested query result
Child relationships never appear in REST responses
As a single string listing all related record names
questions.explain: A child relationship query result is itself a nested query response (totalSize/done/records), which is different from the flat ID value a lookup field holds.

questions.q: How does a Salesforce DateTime field typically appear in a JSON payload?
options: As a Unix timestamp integer
As an ISO 8601 string including both date and time with an offset, e.g. "2026-03-15T14:30:00.000+0000"
As a JSON boolean
As a plain date-only string with no time component
questions.explain: DateTime fields use ISO 8601 strings with both date and time plus a timezone offset; Date-only fields use the shorter date-only ISO 8601 form.

questions.q: Which of these is listed in this lesson as a common payload mistake?
options: Sending a Date value where a DateTime is expected, or vice versa
Including a required field that has no default value
Using lowercase field names instead of the field's actual API name
Sending too few HTTP headers
questions.explain: Mismatching Date vs. DateTime format is called out specifically as a common source of a failed request, alongside omitting a required field and sending the wrong JSON primitive type.
